editions.lead: Hurricane Isaias hit the Florida Panhandle near Destin as a Category 2 storm, leaving hundreds of thousands without power in Florida and Alabama.
Hurricane Isaias strengthened to a Category 3 major hurricane with 120 mph winds hours before an expected Friday-night landfall on the northern Gulf Coast.
Hurricane Isaias, now packing 100 mph winds, is expected to hit the northern Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday, forecasters said.
Isaias became the Atlantic season's first hurricane, and hurricane warnings now cover the coast from Mississippi to the Florida Panhandle.
Tropical Storm Isaias put the northern Gulf Coast under a hurricane watch, with forecasters warning it could hit as a major hurricane late Friday.
Russia's overnight missile and drone attack on Ukraine killed at least 11 people, including five in a Pryluky apartment building, Ukraine's president said.
Drones sank one merchant ship and set another on fire inside Bulgaria's Black Sea economic zone, Bulgaria said; the sunken ship's crew is missing.
Ukraine launched about 650 drones at Moscow overnight, killing two people in one of the largest attacks on the Russian capital in two years, Russian officials said.
The Supreme Court opened its new term by turning away hundreds of appeals, including Second Amendment, COVID vaccine-mandate and "Let's Go Brandon" cases.
Brazil's first-round count has Flavio Bolsonaro leading President Lula, short of a majority, with a runoff on Oct. 25.
France's high-school protests will close up to 500 schools fully or partly Monday, the education minister said; 24 have been burned or ransacked.
A tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an unknown projectile that damaged its engine room, UKMTO said.
Tennessee Corrections Commissioner Frank Strada will resign after the failed lethal injection of Christa Pike.
The G7 agreed to a coordinated release of 100 million barrels, including diesel, starting immediately over four months.
U.S. employers added 29,000 jobs in September and the unemployment rate rose to 4.2%, the Labor Department reported.
The Pentagon is sending about 9,000 sailors and Marines and a third aircraft carrier toward the Middle East.
Treasury and the IRS issued rules implementing the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit for K-12 school choice.
Tennessee halted scheduled executions after Christa Pike appeared still breathing following a lethal injection attempt.
The United States ended its anti-ISIS military mission in Iraq, withdrawing the last U.S. troops after more than two decades.
Iran received a formal U.S. response to its proposal to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
The Education Department finalized a rule rescinding the Biden administration's 2024 Title IX regulations and restoring the 2020 rules; it was announced Sept. 28 and published Sept. 29.
President Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the war.
